input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the input only on `"\n"` (see `const lines = text.split("\n");` in src/ingest/parser.ts) without stripping a trailing `\r`. Files exported from Windows tools use CRLF line endings, so each line (including the header) ends with an extra `\r` character. That throws off the column count comparison against the header and triggers `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row...") — and since the header itself is affected, it's reported starting at row 1. The fix is to normalize line endings (e.g. strip `\r` or split on `/\r?\n/`) before parsing rows.
